newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks up on foreign buying, short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks up on foreign buying, short-covering.

text.p: Delhi shares climbed in early trading on Tuesday as foreign institutional investors continued heavy purchases and speculators covered short positions, brokers said.
After 30 minutes of trading, the Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index was up 4.86 points to 902.65.
Traders said resumption of buying by India's largest mutual fund, the Unit Trust of India, boosted confidence.
"Shortage of floating stocks of blue chip companies in the market in view of annual book closures fuelled speculative buying," Harish Malhotra of stock brokers Malhotra Financial Services said.
Institutional and speculative purchases pushed up Reliance Industries by 2.45 rupees to 374.
ITC Ltd rose eight rupees to 563.
